title: A Crying Kid Started the Turkey Pardon
sources: Smithsonian Magazine, 'The History of Pardoning Turkeys Began With Tad Lincoln': in 1863 a live turkey was sent to the White House for a holiday dinner; Lincoln's son Tad, about ten, named it Jack and made it a pet; when told it would be killed, Tad tearfully pleaded and Lincoln wrote a reprieve, and the turkey was spared

Snopes, 'Turkey Pardon' and UNC Law Library, 'Saved from Fowl Play: a Brief History of Turkey Pardoning': the Tad Lincoln story is the earliest pardon tale; the formal annual presidential pardon became official in 1989
President Lincoln's Cottage (lincolncottage.org): Tad Lincoln and the turkey Jack
